rv.q: The Coast Starlight is the sort of play that will stick in your mind long afterward.

With an excellent ensemble cast, ingenious set, and an empathy-quotient that feels like a balm in the current climate, this is a train journey that will inspire and delight the most reluctant travelers.
Tyne Rafaeli’s direction is also a kinetic marvel.
Bunin is a thought provoking playwright, however this production, directed by Tyne Rafaeli feels verbose, and lacking movement.
However, The Coast Starlight chugs along at a snail’s pace.
The lyrical, Wilder-evoking dénouement owes as much (and perhaps more) to the exquisite Lincoln Center Theater production, directed by Tyne Rafaeli, as to Bunin’s writing.

cn.t: Critics find this train journey drama a mostly pleasant ride, praising the ensemble cast and empathetic tone, though some feel the pace lags and the experimental structure doesn't fully deliver on its premise.
